SMTO-EXE-0223 — SMTO couldn't find that Docker container

GUID: 409a46f2-53fa-5c0b-a943-990f8fbb4cd2
Slug: docker-container-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO looked for the container you named (a program Docker runs) on the Gateway computer, but none has exactly that name or ID right now. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list all Docker containers on that Gateway, including stopped ones. The name must match exactly; SMTO doesn't accept partial names or shortened IDs.
  2. Check that you picked the right Gateway for this conversation; the container may be on a different computer. SMTO only looks on the Gateway you selected.
  3. If the container was removed or recreated earlier, use the current container's exact name, and only ask SMTO to create a new one if you really need it. A recreated container gets a new ID, so the old one no longer matches.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the container by its exact name and finishes the action.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the container name, to the person who manages Docker on that computer. Don't ask SMTO to create a replacement until you know whether an earlier request already did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Exact container resolution on the Gateway found no container whose full ID or exact name matches, or the Docker Engine returned 404 for the container endpoint.

What this means

  • Exact container lookup found no complete-ID/name match, or the Engine returned a container-path not-found response. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Exact container lookup found no complete-ID/name match, or the Engine returned a container-path not-found response.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current container inventory on the same Engine and the original operation before assuming a prior create failed.

How to fix it

  • List containers including stopped ones on the same Gateway (docker ps -a --no-trunc as the Gateway account) and pass the complete container ID or exact name; shortened IDs are never resolved. Confirm the selected Gateway is the host that owns the container, and check any earlier create or remove result before issuing a new change.
  • Select the exact current container from the intended Engine; inspect any earlier create/remove result before new mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended current container resolves by complete ID or one exact unique name.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
